case_name: US Airways Flight 1549 - Hudson River Ditching
situation_summary: Shortly after departure, the aircraft encountered birds and suffered near-total loss of thrust in both engines. The crew assessed available options and executed a controlled ditching on the Hudson River.
system_lesson: When a severe event occurs shortly after departure, decision support should rapidly compare return-to-origin, nearby airport, and non-airport emergency landing options based on time, altitude, glide feasibility, terrain, traffic, and congestion.

decision_pattern.main_decision: Select safest reachable landing option under extreme time pressure

how_nas_pulse_uses_it: Flag bird strike or dual-engine-loss scenarios as time-critical
Prioritize nearest safe landing/diversion candidate analysis
Avoid recommending long reroutes during low-altitude emergency scenarios
Explain that the system is providing historical analogy only, not pilot instructions
source_note: Historical aviation case used for demo analogy only.

case_name: British Airways Flight 009 - Volcanic Ash Encounter
situation_summary: The aircraft flew into volcanic ash, leading to failure of all four engines. The crew descended, exited the ash cloud, restarted engines, and diverted.
system_lesson: Weather hazards are not only storms. The system should treat volcanic ash, smoke, and airborne contamination zones as severe no-fly constraints and generate avoidance corridors.

decision_pattern.main_decision: Exit hazardous airspace and divert to a suitable airport

how_nas_pulse_uses_it: Treat ash-like polygons as hard constraints
Recommend route avoidance rather than minor altitude changes
Highlight severe engine-risk hazards differently from normal convective weather
source_note: Historical aviation case used for demo analogy only.

case_name: Air Transat Flight 236 - Fuel Exhaustion Emergency
situation_summary: A fuel leak led to fuel exhaustion and loss of engine power while over the Atlantic. The aircraft diverted and landed in the Azores.
system_lesson: For fuel emergencies, decision support should prioritize nearest suitable airport, remaining range, runway capability, and airspace coordination rather than ordinary delay or fuel-burn optimization.

decision_pattern.main_decision: Select reachable diversion airport under degraded aircraft condition

how_nas_pulse_uses_it: When fuel emergency tags appear, override normal optimization objective
source_note: Historical aviation case used for demo analogy only.

case_name: United Airlines Flight 232 - Hydraulic Failure and Emergency Landing
situation_summary: An uncontained engine failure caused major hydraulic system failure and severe control degradation. The crew coordinated an emergency landing attempt at Sioux City.
system_lesson: When aircraft control is degraded, the airspace system should prioritize traffic clearing, emergency runway preparation, airport response readiness, and simplified routing.

decision_pattern.main_decision: Clear traffic and coordinate emergency airport arrival
alternatives_considered: Prepare emergency response at receiving airport
constraints: Need for runway and emergency services

how_nas_pulse_uses_it: Recommend airport readiness alerts in demo mode
Show downstream airspace impact of emergency priority routing
source_note: Historical aviation case used for demo analogy only.

case_name: Air India-Style Road Landing / Open-Area Pattern
location: User-provided Air India road-landing analogy plus documented open-road/open-area forced-landing patterns
situation_summary: When airport options are not reachable, some emergency decision patterns consider broad, obstacle-light open areas or road-runway-style corridors as last-resort situational context.
system_lesson: Decision support should first exhaust suitable airport options. If none are reachable, it may surface open-area context for dispatcher/controller awareness while avoiding prescriptive landing instructions.

decision_pattern.main_decision: Identify last-resort open-area context when airport options are unreachable

how_nas_pulse_uses_it: Only surface open-area candidates after fuel/endurance rules out airport return or diversion
Keep language as situational context, not landing instruction
Compare open-area context with nearby water-body and airport context
source_note: Hackathon demo pattern inspired by the user-provided Air India road-landing example; verify the exact event source before treating it as a factual historical case.
